adjudication_records.issue_text: String#scrub requires Ruby 2.1+ but the app may run on Ruby 2.0.x targeted in December 2013, causing i.content.scrub to raise NoMethodError unconditionally so feed polling never works at all

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, feed import does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. `String#scrub` is not available on older Rubies (e.g., 2.0 and earlier), so in such runtimes this line would raise `NoMethodError` and break feed polling entirely. The diff introduces this call without any guard or fallback, so the finding is grounded in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:53 import_remote calls open(url).read without requiring 'open-uri' in that code path, so Kernel#open treats the URL as a filename and raises Errno::ENOENT, preventing embedded articles from being retrieved unless another library happens to load open-uri

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb, .import_remote calls `open(url).read` but that file only `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` and does not `require 'open-uri'`. Other code paths (e.g., Jobs::PollFeed) do require 'open-uri', but TopicRetriever#fetch_http calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote` directly without loading open-uri first. Without open-uri, `Kernel#open` won’t handle HTTP URLs and can treat them as file paths, causing failures when retrieving embedded articles.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_top_topics migration modifies an already-committed migration to add force: true, which drops and recreates top_topics (destroying computed metric data) if the migration is re-run; force: true on the new topic_embeds table is the same footgun and leftover iteration scaffolding

adjudication.rationale: The diff does modify an existing migration (`20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`) to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, and the new `CreateTopicEmbeds` migration also uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop an existing table before creating it, so if these migrations are ever re-run (e.g., redo/rollback+re-migrate in some environments) it can destroy existing data in those tables. This is a real, diff-grounded data-safety/maintenance concern, though it typically won’t affect already-migrated production DBs because migrations aren’t re-run automatically.

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed, feed item HTML is taken from `i.content.scrub`, decoded via `CGI.unescapeHTML`, and passed to `TopicEmbed.import` with no sanitization/tag filtering. TopicEmbed.import creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged for `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. The embed view then renders with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any `<script>`, `<iframe>`, event-handler attributes, etc. present in the feed content would be stored and rendered, enabling stored XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The Readability whitelist filters attribute names (href src) not URL schemes, so javascript: URLs like <a href='javascript:alert(1)'> survive import_remote filtering

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` builds `Readability::Document` with `attributes: %w[href src]` and then passes `doc.content` into `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates a post with `cook_method: :raw_html` and stores/render `raw` directly (`Post#cook` returns `raw`, and `embed/best.html.erb` uses `raw post.cooked`). There is no sanitization or URL-scheme validation anywhere in this path (only relative-URL absolutizing), so if `ruby-readability` preserves `href`/`src` values like `javascript:...`, they would be imported and served verbatim, enabling XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs: src.start_with?('/') matches '//cdn.example.com/...' and src.sub(/^\/+/, '') strips both slashes, producing a broken 404 URL

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, both link and image rewriting treat any `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')` as a relative path and then strip *all* leading slashes via `sub(/^\/+/, '')` before prefixing with the article origin (`prefix`). This will also match protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/a.png`, converting them into `#{prefix}/cdn.example.com/a.png`, which is incorrect and will break such resources (404/wrong host).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No cleanup path for orphaned topic_embeds: deleting a topic leaves EmbedController#best raising 500 forever because TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed returns a stale topic id

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `topic_embeds` records keyed by `embed_url` with `topic_id`/`post_id` but no foreign keys or `dependent: :destroy` behavior (see `CreateTopicEmbeds` migration and `TopicEmbed` model). `EmbedController#best` trusts `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` and, when present, unconditionally builds `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` rather than verifying the topic still exists or falling back to enqueueing retrieval. While the diff doesn’t prove the exact 500 behavior (depends on `TopicView`), it does show a stale-ID/orphan scenario is unhandled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A deleted post makes embed.post nil and PostRevisor.new(nil) raises NoMethodError inside the hourly poll job, killing the rest of the feed processing

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, when an embed already exists it does `post = embed.post` and, if the content changed, immediately does `revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!` without checking `post` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Since `belongs_to :post` does not guarantee the referenced post still exists (no FK constraint shown) a deleted post can make `embed.post` return nil, and PostRevisor methods will then call on `@post` (e.g. `@post.acting_user = ...` in lib/post_revisor.rb), raising NoMethodError. Jobs::PollFeed iterates items and calls TopicEmbed.import with no rescue (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), so such an exception would abort the job and stop processing the remaining feed items.

adjudication_records.issue_text: best.html.erb uses invalid ERB close tag <%- end if %>, so template correctness depends on a compile accident and cannot be verified by tests
matched_golden_ids: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify the same underlying issue: the ERB template closes an if block with `end if`, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and should be just `end`, otherwise it can raise during rendering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The embed view layer (best.html.erb, loading.html.erb, layouts/embed.html.erb) has zero rendering verification; the success test mocks TopicView with no posts/topic stubs so the real template is never rendered with realistic data

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new templates (app/views/embed/best.html.erb, loading.html.erb, layouts/embed.html.erb) but the new controller specs (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb) only assert controller behavior/headers and set expectations on TopicView.new without providing a realistic TopicView object (and RSpec controller specs typically don’t render views unless `render_views` is enabled). As written, the specs don’t exercise the templates’ use of `@topic_view.posts`, `@topic_view.topic.url`, `post.user`, etc., so rendering correctness isn’t verified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RSS items without a title flow into PostCreator with title: nil and skip_validations: true, causing either a DB not-null constraint failure with silent retry: false failure or a topic with nil title breaking slug/URL generation

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed, each RSS item is imported via `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` with no guard/default for `i.title` (which can be nil for some feeds). `TopicEmbed.import` then calls `PostCreator.new(... title: title, skip_validations: true, ...)`, explicitly bypassing validations, so a nil title can reach persistence and potentially raise at the DB layer or create an invalid topic/title state. Additionally, the scheduled job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so an exception would cause a non-retried job failure, matching the finding’s concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key in poll_feed.rb is dead code; the skip-unchanged-feed throttle it implies was never built, so every hour all feed items are re-fetched and re-checked even when the feed is byte-identical, wasting work and causing thundering-herd lookups

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined (with a Redis-style cache key name) but never referenced anywhere in the file. The job’s `execute` calls `poll_feed`, which always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items` every run, with no “skip unchanged feed” mechanism implemented in this diff. That’s a real, diff-grounded inefficiency/dead-code issue, though not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The raw_html cook path silently skips Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook), so plugins hooking after_post_cook won't run on imported posts, causing rendering divergence based on import origin

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now returns `raw` early when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the existing `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, self, ...)` call. Imported posts created with `cook_method: :raw_html` (e.g., TopicEmbed.import via PostCreator) therefore won’t trigger `after_post_cook`, causing plugin hooks to behave differently for these posts. This is a diff-grounded compatibility/architecture concern, though it may be intentional given the comment about skipping the rendering pipeline.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The loading state has no terminal failure mode: when retrieval can never succeed (nonexistent embed_by_username user, URL never in feed, Readability throwing on non-HTML), the consumer's page reloads the iframe every 30 seconds indefinitely with unbounded retries for staff via no_throttle

adjudication.rationale: In the failure case where an embed can never be created, the system has an infinite retry loop. `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil. The `loading.html.erb` view then calls `document.location.reload()` every 30 seconds indefinitely, so the iframe will repeatedly hit `/embed/best`, enqueueing a new job each time. Additionally, `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` calls `TopicRetriever.new(..., no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)).retrieve`, and `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` explicitly disables throttling when `@opts[:no_throttle]` is true, enabling unbounded repeated retrieval attempts for staff. There is no terminal error state when retrieval can’t succeed (e.g., `embed_by_username` user missing causes `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` to return early), so this loop persists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The diff edits two already-existing migrations, adding force: true to create_top_topics, which silently drops pre-existing top_topics data in environments where the table already exists while being a no-op where the migrations already ran

adjudication.rationale: The diff does modify an existing migration (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which in Rails will drop/recreate the table if it already exists, potentially causing data loss if that migration is executed in an environment where `top_topics` pre-exists. However, the finding is inaccurate that *two* existing migrations were changed in this way, and in a normal upgrade path already-run migrations won’t re-run, so the risk is conditional rather than a guaranteed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import tool's `category` option and `created_at` preservation silently removed — imports can no longer target a category and lose original post dates, and `disqus import -c` now errors on unknown option

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the Thor `:category` option is removed (`method_option :category...` deleted) and the logic that mapped `options[:category]` to `category_id` is deleted. The import creation also changes from `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which does not pass `created_at` or any category. As a result, `disqus import -c` would now be an unknown option error, and imported topics/posts will no longer preserve the original `created_at` nor target a category.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `force: true` added to pre-existing unrelated migration `create_top_topics` — data-loss hazard that silently drops the `top_topics` table in partially-migrated environments

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `CreateTopTopics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before recreating it. Because this is a pre-existing migration (not a new one), running migrations in an environment where `top_topics` exists but this migration is (re)applied (e.g., inconsistent/partially migrated DB, restored DB without schema_migrations entry) would silently drop `top_topics` and lose data. This is a real data-loss hazard introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Whitespace/EOF-newline churn in unrelated, already-shipped migration `migrate_word_counts.rb` indicating scope-hygiene failure

adjudication.rationale: The diff touches an existing migration `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` only to remove trailing whitespace on a blank line and adjust the EOF newline (`-  ` to `+` and `\ No newline at end of file` removal). This is unrelated to the embedding/feed features and represents scope/format churn rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A complete RSS/ATOM feed-polling subsystem (scheduled job, site settings, gems) bundled into a PR whose stated intent is only embed URL handling and validation

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds a full feed-import/polling subsystem alongside embedding: new gems (`ruby-readability`, `simple-rss` in Gemfile/lock), new scheduled job `Jobs::PollFeed` (hourly recurrence) plus `feed_polling_*` and `embed_by_username` site settings, and integration in `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` (it runs `Jobs::PollFeed` when `feed_polling_enabled?`). That’s a substantial scope addition beyond just embed URL handling/validation, even if the PR’s stated intent isn’t shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously inside a Sidekiq worker, causing blocking, unbounded-latency full-feed fetch on every embed miss with no timeout

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` directly calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (lib/topic_retriever.rb) before falling back to `fetch_http`. `TopicRetriever` is invoked from a Sidekiq job (`Jobs::RetrieveTopic#execute` calls `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`), so this makes a worker perform a synchronous feed fetch via `PollFeed#poll_feed`, which does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all `rss.items`. That’s a concrete latency/throughput/architecture concern introduced by the change. However, it’s not a strictly provable correctness failure from the diff alone (the “no timeout/unbounded” aspect depends on runtime/network behavior and open-uri defaults), so it fits better as an important non-bug review issue than a definite bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `feed_key` in `poll_feed.rb` is dead code — defined and memoized but never called, leftover from unimplemented conditional-GET design

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `def feed_key` is defined and memoized (`@feed_key ||=`) but never referenced anywhere in that file or elsewhere in the provided diff. The polling logic in `poll_feed` directly parses and iterates the feed without using `feed_key`, so this method is dead code (likely from an unimplemented conditional-GET/cache design).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `embed_url` is not validated at request time — host validation happens asynchronously after render, and the only request-time gate is a client-forgeable `Referer` header

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` is accepted without validating its host; the only synchronous access control is `ensure_embeddable`, which checks `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. That Referer header can be spoofed by a client. Host validation of `@embed_url` happens only later in the background job via `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` (called from `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`), meaning the controller will enqueue/render based on an unvalidated `embed_url` at request time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import path inserts `topic_embeds` rows via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link])` with no host validation, breaking the invariant that only embeddable_host URLs are embedded

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Disqus import task to call `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` (lib/tasks/disqus.thor), and `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`TopicEmbed.import` only validate that the URL is http(s) (`return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`) with no check that `URI(url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Elsewhere, embed retrieval is explicitly restricted to `embeddable_host` (`TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`), so this import path can create `topic_embeds` rows for off-host URLs that normal embed retrieval would refuse, undermining that host restriction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Locale key `embed.permalink` is defined but referenced nowhere in the diff — dead translation string

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `embed.permalink` under `config/locales/server.en.yml`, and there is no visible reference to that key in the changed/added files (embed views reference other `embed.*` keys). However, concluding it is a “dead translation string” is not verifiable from this diff alone because the key could be referenced elsewhere in the codebase outside the shown changes; at most it’s “unused in this diff,” which is not a substantive defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `require_dependency 'email/sender'` in `retrieve_topic.rb` job that sends no email — copy-paste require with no traceable requirement

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`, the job begins with `require_dependency 'email/sender'` but the `RetrieveTopic#execute` method only looks up a `User` and calls `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve`; there is no reference to `Email::Sender` or any mail-sending logic. This makes the require look like an unnecessary copy/paste dependency (extra load/coupling) rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:37 — `i.content.scrub` crashes with NoMethodError on any RSS 2.0 feed that lacks `content:encoded` (nil.scrub), aborting the entire hourly poll mid-loop; with retry: false the failure is silent and later items are never imported

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is nil for an item (e.g., feeds that don’t provide a content field that SimpleRSS maps to `content`), this will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil.scrub`, aborting the job during `rss.items.each`. Since the job has `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the failure won’t be retried, and remaining items in that poll run won’t be imported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:9 + app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9 — format-drift between PollFeed's `embed_url = i.link` and the embed controller's literal discourseEmbedUrl string (query params, trailing slashes, shortened links) combined with exact string matching in `topic_id_for_embed` produces duplicate topics for the same article; no URL normalization at either write site

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` doing an exact string lookup (`where(embed_url: embed_url)`), and `TopicEmbed.import` creates/uniqueness-scopes embeds solely by that exact `embed_url` string (with a unique DB index on `embed_url`). However, multiple code paths can supply semantically-identical but text-different URLs: the embed JS/controller uses a literal `discourseEmbedUrl` passed as `embed_url` param, while feed import uses `i.link` (or `i.id`) from RSS, and remote import uses the provided URL as-is. There is no normalization/canonicalization (trailing slashes, query params, shortened/alternate forms), so the same article can map to different `embed_url` strings and create separate TopicEmbed rows/topics, i.e., duplicates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:46 and poll_feed.rb:36 — `open(uri)` with no timeout and no size cap on both fetch paths; a hung upstream host blocks a Sidekiq worker indefinitely and one slow site can exhaust the worker pool, with no circuit breaker or fallback

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two network fetch paths that call `open` from open-uri without any timeout/limits: `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read` (invoked from `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`). With no `read_timeout`/`open_timeout` (or equivalent) and no response size cap, a slow/hung upstream can block a Sidekiq worker indefinitely and potentially exhaust the worker pool, which is an availability defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:7 + app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb — no terminal failure state creates an unbounded retry loop: the loading view reloads every 30s, each reload enqueues another RetrieveTopic, and permanently failing imports are re-fetched forever (every 60s throttle window) for every embedded page

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The loading template unconditionally reloads the page every 30s (`setTimeout(... document.location.reload(), 30000)` in app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), so the same request path will run again and enqueue another `RetrieveTopic`. There is no persisted “failed”/terminal state in `TopicRetriever`/`TopicEmbed` to stop re-attempts when fetching/parsing/importing fails; `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` will keep reaching `fetch_http` as long as no `TopicEmbed` exists. The only backoff shown is a 60s Redis throttle in `retrieved_recently?`, so permanently failing URLs can be retried indefinitely (roughly once per minute) while the embedded page keeps reloading forever.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:38 — synchronous inline invocation of `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inside a per-URL retrieval job bypasses the scheduled job's retry: false semantics and means a single embed page view imports topics for every item in the feed; the two entry points have different retry and concurrency behavior

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb` `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. From the diff, `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` parses the configured feed and iterates `rss.items.each`, calling `TopicEmbed.import(...)` for every item, not just the current `@embed_url`. Because this is invoked from the per-URL retrieval path, it can cause a single `TopicRetriever` run (triggered via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`) to perform a full feed import, and it bypasses Sidekiq scheduling/job options (e.g., the `sidekiq_options retry: false` on the scheduled job won’t apply because the work isn’t executed as that scheduled Sidekiq job). This is a concrete behavior/performance/architecture concern grounded in the diff, though not an outright correctness failure since `TopicEmbed` dedupes by `embed_url`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/post.rb:131-133 — the `raw_html` short-circuit `return raw` executes before `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`, so plugins registered on after_post_cook silently never run for imported posts with no way to detect or opt into this path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` before `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` (app/models/post.rb). This means posts created with `cook_method: :raw_html` (e.g., TopicEmbed.import via PostCreator in app/models/topic_embed.rb) will bypass the `:after_post_cook` plugin hook entirely. That behavior is verifiably introduced by the diff, but it appears intentional to skip the rendering pipeline for raw HTML rather than an outright correctness defect; the concern is about plugin extensibility/visibility for this new code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:18-20 — `feed_key` (and its supporting `require 'digest/sha1'`) is dead code; the conditional-fetch/If-Modified-Since design it implies was never implemented so the feed is fully re-fetched and every item re-processed hourly

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `require 'digest/sha1'` is only used by the `feed_key` method, and `feed_key` is never referenced anywhere in the diff. The job does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates all `rss.items` every run, so there is no conditional-fetch/If-Modified-Since logic implemented despite what `feed_key` suggests. However, this is primarily dead/unused code and an efficiency/architecture concern (items are still iterated even if `TopicEmbed.import` may no-op/update based on `embed_url` and `content_sha1`), not a directly verifiable correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:28-31 — the update branch revises only the post body via PostRevisor; the topic title from `i.title` is never updated, so a corrected headline in the feed never propagates and the topic shows a stale title with fresh body

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the creation path uses the passed `title` when calling `PostCreator.new(user, title: title, ...)`, but in the update path (`else` branch) it only calls `PostRevisor#revise!` with the new raw content (`absolutize_urls(url, contents)`) and never updates the topic/post title. Since `import` is invoked from `Jobs::PollFeed` with `i.title`, a changed/corrected feed title would be ignored while the body updates, leaving a stale title with fresh content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:65-73 — `absolutize_urls` mangles protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/img.png` becomes `http://site.com/cdn.example.com/img.png`) and drops ports on scheme mismatches (`https://host:80` becomes `https://host`), breaking CDN assets in embeds

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the condition `href.start_with?('/')` / `src.start_with?('/')` treats protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png` as relative paths and rewrites them to `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`, producing `http(s)://host/cdn.example.com/img.png` (mangled). Also, `prefix` only appends the port when `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`, so a URL like `https://host:80/...` loses `:80` even though 80 is non-default for https, changing the resulting absolute URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:26-30 — `setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is non-atomic; a crash between the two redis calls leaves `retrieved:<url>` with no TTL, permanently disabling retrieval for that article

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only then TTL is set via a separate `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes (or connection drops) after setnx but before expire, `retrieved:<url>` can persist without a TTL, causing `retrieved_recently?` to return `true` forever and permanently blocking retrieval for that embed URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — editing an already-shipped migration to add `force: true` in an unrelated feature diff; a re-run silently drops the existing top_topics table and data, and modifying released migrations desynchronizes environments that already applied the original

adjudication.rationale: The diff edits an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb`, changing `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before recreating it, which can silently destroy existing `top_topics` data if this migration is (re)run (e.g., during redo/reset or on a database where the table already exists). Modifying an already-present migration also risks divergent behavior across environments that previously applied the original version.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:10 — `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` raises RecordNotFound → 500 when the topic is deleted but the TopicEmbed row survives (no dependent-destroy, no FK constraint), breaking every blog page embedding that article instead of degrading to the start-discussion path

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns a `topic_id`, the code unconditionally does `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` with no check that the topic still exists or rescue path. The diff also creates `topic_embeds` without any FK constraint and `TopicEmbed` has `belongs_to :topic`/`:post` with no `dependent:` behavior shown, so orphaned `topic_embeds` rows are possible if the topic/post is deleted. In that case, this code path can raise (likely `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`) and return a 500 instead of falling back to the "loading/start discussion" path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Post#cook raw_html early return skips Markdown rendering, Discourse HTML sanitization (tag/attribute whitelisting, javascript: URL scrubbing), and Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook), so unsanitized RSS feed content from feed_polling_url is stored verbatim and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view, enabling stored XSS against all embed viewers

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a `raw_html` cook path that bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline: `Post#cook` now does `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, skipping `post_analyzer.cook(*args)` and `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. Feed/RSS imports set this mode (`PostCreator.new(... cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])` in `TopicEmbed.import`), and `Jobs::PollFeed` passes untrusted `i.content` from `feed_polling_url` into `TopicEmbed.import` with only `CGI.unescapeHTML(...).scrub` plus URL absolutization (no HTML tag/attribute sanitization). The embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so malicious HTML/JS from the feed can become stored and executed for all embed viewers (stored XSS) within the embed frame.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import silently removed the --category CLI option, breaking existing invocations with Thor's 'Unknown option' error, and changed imported topic bodies from permalink stubs to full scraped article HTML stored as raw_html (exposing the finding-1 XSS surface via the Disqus path) with all topics landing in the default category

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the Thor CLI option `--category` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` (deleted `method_option :category` and all `category_id` handling). Any existing invocation passing `--category` will now raise Thor’s “Unknown option” error, and imported topics will no longer be assigned to a specified category. Additionally, the Disqus import behavior changes from creating a stub body with just a permalink (`PostCreator.new(... raw: "[[Permalink](...)]" ...)`) to `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which fetches/scrapes the remote article (`Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`) and imports it as `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `raw_html` (skipping the normal cooking pipeline). That is a real behavior change and can expand exposure to unsanitized HTML depending on upstream content/filters.

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true added to already-shipped migration 20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb causes any replayed migration to silently DROP existing top_topics data, leaking a development convenience into a shared migration

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` drops the table if it already exists before recreating it, so if this migration is ever replayed (e.g., migrated down/up, or run in an environment where the table already exists), it can silently destroy existing `top_topics` data. That is a real data-loss risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb uses i.content which is nil for RSS 2.0 feeds (which use description instead), causing nil.scrub NoMethodError that kills the poller for the exact feed format the setting promises, with retry: false so no retry occurs

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the code unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` inside `rss.items.each`. If `i.content` is nil (e.g., for some feeds/items that don't provide a `content` field), this will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil.scrub` and abort the poller. This is especially problematic given `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so a single such item/feed would cause the job to fail without retries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_url is matched by exact string comparison against the feed's i.link, so trailing slashes or query string differences (e.g. ?utm_source=feed) cause lookup misses and duplicate topics with identical content, fragmenting discussion across two topics

adjudication.rationale: The diff stores and looks up embeds by exact string equality on `embed_url` (`TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` in `TopicEmbed.import` and `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first` in `topic_id_for_embed`). In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the URL comes directly from the feed item (`url = i.link` or `i.id`) with no canonicalization/normalization. Therefore variations like trailing slashes or tracking query params would not match the previously stored `embed_url`, causing `embed.blank?` and creating a new topic/embed instead of updating the existing one, fragmenting discussion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook_method is accepted from arbitrary PostCreator opts with no whitelist, gating setting, or audit marker, turning the raw_html sanitization bypass into a public API and general-purpose stored-XSS primitive in the core post-creation path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new bypass path: `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb), and `PostCreator#setup_post` now directly assigns `post.cook_method = @opts[:cook_method]` when present (lib/post_creator.rb) with no internal gating/whitelist. This does expand the core post-creation API to allow callers to opt into unsanitized HTML, but the diff does not show any controller/param path that lets arbitrary users supply `cook_method`, so the claimed "public API" stored-XSS primitive is plausible but not directly verifiable from the shown changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: remote content imported and rendered as raw HTML with no sanitization — the cook_method == raw_html path returns raw strings verbatim, the RSS path applies no tag/attribute filtering and CGI.unescapeHTML re-activates entity-encoded payloads, the readability path whitelists tag/attribute names but not URL schemes allowing javascript: URLs, and the result is rendered unescaped via raw post.cooked in embed views and the forum UI

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` mode where `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline (`return raw if cook_method == ...` in `app/models/post.rb`). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts from remote RSS/readability content with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `skip_validations: true` (`lib/topic_embed.rb`), and the RSS path explicitly unescapes HTML entities (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`). `import_remote` uses `Readability::Document` allowing `a/img` with `href/src` attributes but does not show any URL-scheme filtering, and `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative URLs, leaving `javascript:` etc. intact. The embed view renders HTML unescaped via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`). Together this is a verifiable stored XSS vector introduced by the raw_html bypass for remotely-sourced content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: HTML/script injection via unescaped URL interpolated into the import footer in TopicEmbed — the RSS item link is only regex-checked to start with http(s):// and never URI-parsed or escaped, allowing attribute breakout and executable content in the raw_html post

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the footer HTML is built by interpolating `url` directly into an `#{url}` string (`contents << ... I18n.t(... link: "#{url}")`). The only validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes, spaces, or other characters that can break out of the single-quoted `href` attribute or inject HTML/JS into the link text. Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for that mode, this unescaped HTML will be rendered, enabling script/HTML injection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SSRF via redirect-following fetch — invalid_host? validates only the initial URL host, but open-uri follows 3xx redirects by default, so an open redirect lets the Discourse server fetch arbitrary internal addresses and render the responses to viewers

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`, which only validates the *initial* `@embed_url` host (`SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`). But the actual fetch uses `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (and `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `Jobs::PollFeed`), and `open-uri` follows HTTP 3xx redirects by default. This means an allowed external URL on `embeddable_host` could redirect to an internal/localhost URL, causing the server to fetch it (SSRF) and then import/display the fetched content via `TopicEmbed.import(...)` and the embed views (`raw post.cooked`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer header used as access control in EmbedController — the fully client-controlled header gates the endpoint, making the embed policy unenforceable and allowing unauthenticated fetch-job flooding since the retrieved_recently? throttle is keyed on the full URL and can be bypassed by varying the path, enabling unbounded outbound requests and Sidekiq queue flooding

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is gated solely by `request.referer` (`URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), which is a client-controlled header and can be trivially spoofed by non-browser clients; this makes the embed policy unenforceable from the server side. When no embed exists, `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)` without any authentication check shown in the diff, so an attacker can repeatedly hit `/embed/best?embed_url=...` (with a forged Referer) to enqueue many `RetrieveTopic` jobs. The throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` is keyed on the full `@embed_url` (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so varying the path/query on the same allowed host bypasses throttling and can drive unbounded outbound fetches (`TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)` uses `open(url)`) and Sidekiq queue growth.

adjudication_records.issue_text: postMessage origin check in embed.js uses substring indexOf instead of strict equality, accepting any message whose origin appears anywhere in discourseUrl — currently only affects the discourse-resize message (layout manipulation via unvalidated height), but the pattern invites future message types to inherit a broken origin check
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same core vulnerability: the postMessage origin validation relies on indexOf/substring matching rather than strict origin equality, allowing malicious domains containing the trusted domain string (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com) to bypass the check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:35-43: Every behavioral test stubs the unit's own internals (perform_retrieve, retrieved_recently?), so the real TopicRetriever logic including the Redis throttle and perform_retrieve/fetch_http is never executed; inverted throttle or dropped expire would keep the suite green — a tautological spec

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the “valid host” examples stub TopicRetriever’s own methods: they set expectations on `perform_retrieve` and stub `retrieved_recently?` (lines ~35-43), so neither the Redis throttle logic in `retrieved_recently?` (setnx/expire) nor the actual `perform_retrieve` path (`PollFeed`/`fetch_http`/`import_remote`) is ever executed by these behavioral tests. This makes the spec largely tautological and unable to catch regressions like a broken throttle/expire.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:44-57: The success tests never render any template (rspec-rails controller specs don't render views by default, TopicView is mocked to nil), so best.html.erb, loading.html.erb, and layouts/embed.html.erb are never compiled or executed; a template that raises on first real render ships with a green spec

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the controller specs use `get :best` without `render_views`, so rspec-rails will not compile/render best.html.erb/loading.html.erb/layouts/embed.html.erb. Additionally, in the "creates a topic view" example `TopicView.expects(:new)...` sets an expectation but does not specify a return value, so `@topic_view` may be nil in the controller while still producing a green spec (since views aren’t rendered). This is a diff-grounded test coverage gap for the newly added embed templates, not a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8-27: The error tests assert only response.should_not be_success, which cannot distinguish the claimed failure from any other; the 'is 404 without an embed_url' test never asserts 404 (params.require raises ParameterMissing mapped to 400), and the other error tests pass on a plain 500 even if the rescues are removed or broken

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly points out weak/ambiguous assertions in the newly added specs. In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the “is 404 without an embed_url” example only checks `response.should_not be_success` and never asserts a 404; meanwhile the controller action calls `params.require(:embed_url)` (`EmbedController#best`), which will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` (typically mapped to 400), so the test description is inconsistent and the status isn’t verified. Similarly, the other error-path tests (missing host / no referer) also only assert “not success”, so they would still pass on an unhandled exception/500 if error handling changed or broke. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test quality issue rather than an application defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:44-50: The 'tells the topic retriever to work' test verifies only that a mocked TopicRetriever#retrieve was invoked; it never asserts the enqueued job's arguments (user_id, embed_url) nor that the loading template is rendered, so user_id threading that drives the staff no_throttle path is undetectable

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` is found it does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` and `render 'loading'`. The spec at `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` (the “tells the topic retriever to work…” example) only mocks/asserters a `TopicRetriever#retrieve` call and does not assert (a) that the `retrieve_topic` job is enqueued with the expected `user_id`/`embed_url` args nor (b) that the `loading` template is rendered, so it wouldn’t validate the user_id threading relevant to the staff `no_throttle` behavior in `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:8-39: All four tests stub poller.expects(:poll_feed), so #poll_feed itself (RSS/Atom ingestion, SimpleRSS parsing, CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub), TopicEmbed.import delegation) and #feed_key are never executed; with sidekiq retry: false, a crash inside poll_feed breaks the production hourly job silently with no test failure

adjudication.rationale: The spec file only tests `Jobs::PollFeed#execute` gating logic and, in each example, sets an expectation on `poll_feed` (never/once) instead of exercising `poll_feed` itself. As a result, the newly added ingestion logic in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and `TopicEmbed.import(...)`) and `#feed_key` are not covered by these tests. This is a concrete test-coverage gap for nontrivial new code. The claim that failures would be "silent" is overstated (Sidekiq would log errors), but the lack of tests for the risky parsing/import path is valid.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:43-46: The content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1 guard in TopicEmbed.import is only exercised on its true side; no test imports identical unchanged content and asserts no revision occurs, so if the sha1 comparison is dropped or inverted every hourly poll pushes every feed item through PostRevisor with bypass_rate_limiter: true and no test fails

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path only calls `PostRevisor` when `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` (see the `else` branch where it compares and then `revisor.revise!(..., bypass_rate_limiter: true)`). The spec `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` does exercise the update path only with changed content (`"muhahaha new contents!"`), and does not cover the unchanged-content case to assert that `PostRevisor` is *not* invoked and `content_sha1` is not rewritten. That’s a concrete missing-test gap around nontrivial logic that could allow an accidental inversion/removal of the guard without test failure, potentially causing every poll to revise posts unnecessarily.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:8-48: TopicEmbed.import_remote (Readability extraction, opts[:title] || doc.title fallback, tag/attribute whitelist) is never exercised by the model's own spec, despite the disqus import task being rewritten to depend on it as its sole import path; a wrong tags whitelist or broken doc.title fallback silently produces empty or title-less topics

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (uses `ruby-readability` to fetch/parse remote HTML with a tags/attributes whitelist and `opts[:title] || doc.title` fallback) in `app/models/topic_embed.rb`, and rewrites the Disqus import task to rely on it exclusively (`lib/tasks/disqus.thor` now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`). However, `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` only exercises `.import` (creation/update, URL validation, absolutize_urls) and never calls `.import_remote`, so regressions in the Readability extraction, whitelist, or title fallback would not be caught by the model spec. This is a concrete missing-test gap for new nontrivial logic, not a demonstrated runtime defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:43-46: The new skip_validations option in PostRevisor#revise! is passed by the update test, but the test's revision content is fully valid so nothing verifies validations are actually skipped; if the flag were inverted (validate: @opts[:skip_validations]) the existing test still passes

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new behavior in PostRevisor#update_post: `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`. TopicEmbed.import’s update path calls `revisor.revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)`, and the spec `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb` “Supports updating the post” exercises that path but only asserts the cooked content changes. It does not assert that validations were actually skipped (e.g., by making the revision invalid), so an inverted implementation like `validate: @opts[:skip_validations]` could still allow the test to pass. This is a test coverage gap tied to newly introduced logic, not a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `force: true` added to already-shipped migration create_top_topics.rb makes it destructive on re-run, silently dropping the top_topics table and its data via DROP TABLE IF EXISTS with no backup or rollback

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails/ActiveRecord, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists (effectively `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS`) before creating it, which can silently delete existing `top_topics` data if this migration is ever re-run (e.g., migrate:redo/reset or running migrations against a DB that already has the table).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `force: true` in create_topic_embeds.rb can silently drop the embed_url→topic_id mapping on re-run, causing duplicate topics to be created on subsequent feed polls since the mapping is the only dedupe key

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, which will drop and recreate the table if it already exists, wiping the `embed_url` uniqueness mapping and any stored `content_sha1`. That is a real data-loss footgun in the migration definition, but it’s not a runtime defect in normal production operation because Rails migrations are only applied once (tracked in `schema_migrations`) and won’t “re-run” unless someone explicitly loads schema or manually reruns/forces it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embeds lacks foreign keys and no destroy hook on Topic/Post deletion, leaving orphaned topic_embeds rows that permanently break import and embed serving (TopicView on nonexistent topic, NoMethodError in PostRevisor)

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` defines `topic_id`/`post_id` as plain integers with no foreign keys, and the `TopicEmbed` model only has `belongs_to :topic`/`:post` with no visible dependent-destroy cleanup on topic/post deletion. The code later assumes these references exist: `EmbedController#best` uses `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` and then `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` without checking the topic still exists, and `TopicEmbed.import` update path does `post = embed.post` then `PostRevisor.new(post)` which would error if `post` was deleted (nil). Orphaned `topic_embeds` rows can therefore cause broken embed serving/import behavior if topics/posts are removed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import rewritten to use TopicEmbed.import_remote with live HTTP fetches per thread, aborting mid-migration on dead/moved links and creating duplicate topics on re-run since old imports lack topic_embeds rows

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the import now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` instead of creating a post from the Disqus-exported data. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does a live `open(url).read` with no error handling, so a dead/moved link will raise and can abort the entire Thor import mid-run. Also, `TopicEmbed.import` only de-duplicates via `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url)`; topics/posts created by the previous Disqus importer would not have `topic_embeds` rows at all, so re-running the importer after this change would not detect existing topics and can create duplicates for the same `t[:link]`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb crashes with NoMethodError on nil.scrub when a feed item lacks a content element (description-only RSS feeds), and retry: false silently halts all feed imports for that feed

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks a `content` field (common in description-only RSS), `i.content` can be nil, making `nil.scrub` raise `NoMethodError`, crashing the job. Additionally, `sidekiq_options retry: false` means such failures won’t be retried for that run, so imports for that feed won’t proceed until a future scheduled run (and will keep failing if the feed remains description-only).

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed poll loop has no per-item error isolation, so a single bad item kills the entire poll job mid-loop

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), the code iterates `rss.items.each do |i|` and directly processes each item (`i.link`/`i.id`, `i.content.scrub`, `CGI.unescapeHTML`, `TopicEmbed.import(...)`) without any per-item `begin/rescue`. Any exception raised by a single malformed item (e.g., missing `content`, invalid encoding causing `scrub`/parse issues, etc.) will abort the entire job mid-loop. With `sidekiq_options retry: false`, this can permanently skip remaining items until the next run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 feed items because SimpleRSS only populates content from atom:content while RSS 2.0 items expose description, causing NoMethodError at `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If `i.content` is `nil` for any feed item, this will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil.scrub` and abort the polling job. The diff shows no nil-guard or fallback (e.g., `i.description`), so feeds/items without `content` will break importing. The specific claim about SimpleRSS + RSS2 vs Atom is plausible but not provable from the diff; the nil dereference itself is directly verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `i.title` nil flows into `title: nil`, causing a not-null DB violation

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, each RSS item is imported via `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` with no fallback when `i.title` is missing/nil. `TopicEmbed.import` then passes `title: title` into `PostCreator.new(...)` while also setting `skip_validations: true`, so a nil title can reach persistence without being caught by model validations, potentially triggering an error when creating the topic/post if the underlying title field is required at the DB/model level.

adjudication_records.issue_text: With `sidekiq_options retry: false`, a failed poll job leaves all feeds after the first bad item unimported, reruns hourly dying on the same item forever, and only leaves a sidekiq dead-set entry while the scheduler appears healthy

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false` and then iterates `rss.items.each` without any per-item error handling. If any item processing (e.g., `open(...)`, `SimpleRSS.parse`, `i.content.scrub`, or `TopicEmbed.import`) raises, the whole job will abort and subsequent items in that run won’t be imported. That robustness concern is grounded in the diff. However, claims about “dead-set entry” and the scheduler “appears healthy” are Sidekiq/runtime-behavior specifics not directly verifiable from the diff alone, and the “forever” aspect depends on the feed repeatedly presenting the same failing item.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed rows are never cleaned up when their topic or post is deleted, leaving dangling rows

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `topic_embeds` with `topic_id`/`post_id` `null: false` but no foreign keys or cascading deletes in the migration, and `TopicEmbed` only declares `belongs_to :topic`/`:post` without any `dependent:` behavior shown anywhere. If a `Topic` or `Post` is deleted, nothing in this diff ensures the corresponding `TopicEmbed` row is removed, which can leave orphans that will still be returned by `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` (used by `EmbedController#best`) and can also block re-import due to the unique index on `embed_url`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: When a TopicEmbed references a deleted topic, `topic_id_for_embed` returns the dead topic_id and `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)` raises, causing the embed to 500 or 404 in the iframe permanently

adjudication.rationale: `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` is implemented as `where(embed_url: embed_url).pluck(:topic_id).first`, with no check that the referenced `Topic` still exists. In `EmbedController#best`, when `topic_id` is present it unconditionally does `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})`. Since the diff also adds a `topic_embeds` table with `topic_id`/`post_id` but no foreign keys or dependent cleanup, a dangling `topic_embeds` row pointing at a deleted topic is possible, and the controller has no guard/rescue for that case, so the embed endpoint can error rather than re-enqueue retrieval/render loading.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` early-returns because the dangling `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:).exists?` is true, so a broken embed can never self-heal

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, the `return if TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` guard is an intentional short-circuit to avoid re-fetching once an embed record exists. The diff does not define or demonstrate a "broken embed" state that should trigger re-retrieval, nor does it show a dangling/partial `TopicEmbed` being created (creation happens inside a transaction and only after a `post` is present). The claim that embeds can "never self-heal" is speculative and not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In the PollFeed update path, `embed.post` is nil for a dangling TopicEmbed, so `PostRevisor.new(nil)` raises NoMethodError and kills the poll job

adjudication.rationale: `Jobs::PollFeed` calls `TopicEmbed.import(...)`. In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed is found (`embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first`), it assigns `post = embed.post` and, if the content has changed, does `revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)` with no nil-guard. If the `topic_embeds` row is dangling (e.g., `post_id` points to a missing post), `embed.post` will be `nil`, and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` will raise, aborting the poll job. The diff introduces this code path and does not defend against a missing associated post.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fire-and-forget retrieval in embed/loading.html.erb has no failure state: if retrieval fails (SocketError, empty Readability content, blank title), no TopicEmbed is created, no error surfaces in the iframe, and the user sees an infinite 'Loading Discussion...' loop

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `TopicEmbed` exists it always enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders `embed/loading` (no alternate branch). `embed/loading.html.erb` unconditionally reloads every 30s, so if the background retrieval never creates a `TopicEmbed` (e.g., `TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses `open(url).read` and `Readability::Document` without any rescue/validation and can raise or return unusable content, causing `creator.create` to return nil and no embed row to be created), the iframe will remain in the loading page indefinitely and keep re-enqueuing jobs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Throttle key in TopicRetriever is committed before the work succeeds: `retrieved_recently?` sets the redis key before `perform_retrieve` runs, so a failed fetch burns the 60-second window and all retry enqueues no-op, extending the user-visible stall to 60s+ with nothing logged

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, `retrieved_recently?` is called before `perform_retrieve` and, on first call, it commits the throttle (`$redis.setnx` + `expire 60`) and returns `false`, allowing `perform_retrieve` to run. If `perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http` fails (e.g., `open(@embed_url)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` raises), the redis key remains set and subsequent calls within 60s will return `true` and skip `perform_retrieve`, effectively suppressing immediate retries/work despite the previous attempt failing. This behavior is directly implied by the ordering and lack of rescue/rollback around the redis key in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` runs unconditionally after `revisor.revise!` without checking the return value, so when revise! returns false the sha1 still advances and every future poll hash-matches and skips the update, leaving the imported article permanently stale

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`, it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then immediately does `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` with no conditional on whether the revise succeeded. The diff shows `PostRevisor#revise!` can return `false` (`return false if not should_revise?`), so it’s possible for the post not to be updated while the SHA1 is advanced, causing subsequent polls to think content matches and skip future updates (stale imported content).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Outbound fetches (`open(url).read`) have no timeout override and no download size cap, and `TopicEmbed.import` calls PostCreator with `skip_validations: true`, bypassing maximum-post-length validation, so unbounded content is read into memory and written to the posts table

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple outbound fetches via Ruby's `open-uri` without any explicit `open_timeout`, `read_timeout`, or size limiting: `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` and `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `Jobs::PollFeed`. Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `PostCreator.new(... skip_validations: true, ...)`, and the update path calls `PostRevisor#revise!` with `skip_validations: true`; `PostRevisor` is modified to honor this by doing `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`. This makes it possible for very large remote content to be read into memory and persisted while bypassing model validations (including any length/size validations that would normally apply), which is a real security/robustness issue grounded in the added code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` in TopicEmbed.import silently drops feed items whose link is blank or whose id is a urn:uuid, and poll_feed's fallback mostly produces non-http ids that hit this silent return, resulting in zero imported topics with zero diagnostics logged

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, each item’s `url` is set to `i.link`, but if it’s blank or not http(s) it falls back to `i.id` (`url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`).
